full_judgment:
12. PW 8 Gohar Ali stated in his evidence that at the time of occurrence he was in the field of Bhatirbond to see his own plot. All on a sudden he heard some alarm and advanced towards the place of occurrence, he saw some 5/6 persons were beating one man and accused Abdur Razzak, Abdul Khaleque, Madris, Masuk, Shamsuddin and Anu were those persons. They had dao, fala, etc. in their hands. Seeing this horrible condition he felt that his blood pressure was increased and he sat down on his land and after one hour he found that a man was dead and he was taken by a wooden palla and recognised that man to be Ashabudidn and also saw marks of violence on his body. Ashabuddin is the brother of informant Shamshuddin. In his cross- examination he has stated that he has no land of his own but mosjid owned some land. He stated that while he was advancing some 200/300 cubits away his blood pressure was increased and he felt dizzy and thereafter he came back. Thereafter he found Ashabuddin with injuries. He stated that he lives in the house of Ainuddin, uncle of informant Shamsuddin. 

 26. Accused-appellants, namely, Giasuddin, Feroj Ali, Tajul Islam and Rashid are found guilty under section 148 of the Penal Code. Prosecution case states that accused Madris, Khaleque, Masuk, Abdur Razzak, Anu Miah and Shamsuddin at first surrounded the deceased Ashabuddin and inflicted some injuries on his persons. Accused-appellants Giasuddin, Feroj Ali, Tajul Islam and Rashid Ali are charged to have committed rioting being armed with deadly weapon and arrived at the scene of occurrence just immediately after the accused Madris, Khaleque, Masuk, Abdur Razzak, Shamsuddin and Anu Miah had committed the offence as narrated above. The learned Judge misdirected himself in finding the accused-appellants Giasuddin, Feroj Ali, Tajul Islam and Rashid Ali guilty of the offence under section 148 of the Penal Code although he did not find accused-appellants Madris, Khaleque, Abdur Razzak, Masuk, Shamsuddin and Anu Miah guilty of the offence under section 148 of the Penal Code. This is quite discriminatory. We are not at all satisfied that these accused have at all committed the offence of rioting. Therefore, they are to be acquitted on benefit of doubt.
